name: Dietrich Mateschitz
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Mateschitz spent his twenties as a university student (taking 10 years to graduate) and then worked in marketing at Unilever and Blendax. He co-founded Red Bull at age 40 in 1984; no material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Mateschitz was born in Styria, Austria to two schoolteachers who separated when he was young. family_context_summary: Both parents were schoolteachers in Styria, Austria; they separated when he was young, and he lived independently from his teenage years.
evidence_summary: Mateschitz showed no early entrepreneurial milestones. He spent a decade in university, worked in conventional marketing jobs through his twenties and thirties, and only founded Red Bull at age 40 in 1984. His parents were schoolteachers with no business empire to inherit.

name: Kane

name: Andrzej Żuławski
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Żuławski worked as an assistant director to Andrzej Wajda through his early twenties, but his directorial debut came in 1967 at age 27 with two short television films. His first feature film was released in 1971 at age 31; no material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Lviv (then Poland, now Ukraine), Żuławski moved with his diplomat father to France, Czechoslovakia, and Poland. He studied film at IDHEC in Paris (graduating 1965) and philosophy at the Sorbonne and University of Warsaw. He served as assistant director to Andrzej Wajda on several films in the early 1960s.
family_context_summary: His father Mirosław Żuławski was a writer, journalist, and Polish diplomat who served as Poland's representative to UNESCO in Paris. The family moved between France, Czechoslovakia, and Poland during his childhood.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father was a writer and diplomat who co-wrote the screenplay for Żuławski's first feature film, suggesting direct domain transfer in literary and film arts.
evidence_summary: Żuławski had strong family and institutional advantages — his father was a writer-diplomat, and he studied at IDHEC in Paris and assisted Andrzej Wajda — but he did not direct his own film until age 27 in 1967. By 26, he was an assistant director, which is a career step but not a material, independently verifiable milestone as a director.

name: Colin Bell
milestone_by_age_26: Won the English First Division championship with Manchester City in 1968 at age 22 and became an England international, establishing himself as one of the top midfielders in English football well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Bell grew up in Hesleden, County Durham, a mining community in northeast England. He played for Horden Colliery Welfare Juniors and had trials at several clubs before signing professional with Bury in July 1963 at age 17. He became Bury's captain and moved to Manchester City in March 1966 for £45,000, helping them win promotion and then the First Division title in 1968.
family_context_summary: Grew up in a working-class mining community in Hesleden, County Durham. His mother died at age 39 from a bowel tumor. Specific parental occupations not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: professional football pipeline, working-class background, early professional debut, complementary trio
evidence_summary: Bell signed professional with Bury at 17, became captain, and transferred to Manchester City at 20, winning the First Division at 22. He grew up in a northeast England mining community with no documented family football connections. His path was driven by early professional immersion and the elite English football pipeline, complemented by the Bell-Lee-Summerbee trio at Manchester City. Manager Malcolm Allison and Joe Mercer provided crucial guidance.

name: Peter Schmeichel
milestone_by_age_26: Won Danish league titles with Brøndby in 1987, 1988, and 1990, the Danish Cup in 1989, and was named Danish Goalkeeper of the Year (Det Gyldne Bur) multiple times by age 26, establishing himself as Denmark's top goalkeeper before his move to Manchester United.
early_history_summary: Born in Gladsaxe, Copenhagen to a Polish jazz musician father and Danish nurse mother, Schmeichel began playing football at age 8 in 1972. He progressed through Høje-Gladsaxe and Gladsaxe-Hero BK, then played for Hvidovre while working multiple jobs to make ends meet. He joined Brøndby in 1987 and immediately won the Danish league, becoming the dominant goalkeeper in Danish football.
family_context_summary: Father was a Polish jazz musician who immigrated to Denmark; mother was a Danish nurse. The family held Polish nationality until becoming Danish citizens in 1971. Schmeichel worked multiple jobs (textile factory, old people's home, advertising firm) while playing lower-division football.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a musician, not connected to football. No family football domain transfer documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: physical dominance, early football start, immigrant background, multiple jobs, mentor coach
evidence_summary: Schmeichel's exceptional physical attributes (6'4", 100kg) and early start in football (age 8) drove his rise through Danish football. He worked multiple non-football jobs while playing in lower divisions, joining Brøndby at 23 and immediately winning league titles. His father was a Polish jazz musician with no football connections. Coach Svend Aage Hansen at Gladsaxe-Hero was an early mentor who also became his father-in-law.

name: Ronnie James Dio
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Dio performed professionally from age 15 with various bands (Vegas Kings, Ronnie & The Red Caps, Ronnie Dio & The Prophets) and recorded non-charting singles, but achieved no material milestone by age 26. His breakthrough came with Rainbow in 1975 at age 33.
early_history_summary: Born Ronald James Padavona in Portsmouth, New Hampshire to Italian-American parents, Dio grew up in Cortland, New York. He began musical training at age 5 on trumpet and formed his first rock band, The Vegas Kings, in high school in 1957. He performed continuously through the 1960s with various bands, had a club residency at Lake George in 1960, and formed Elf in 1967, but none achieved notable commercial success before his late twenties.
family_context_summary: Born to Italian-American parents Patrick and Anna Padavona in Portsmouth, New Hampshire; family returned to Cortland, New York. Father served in the U.S. Army during WWII. Specific family financial status not documented.
evidence_summary: Dio was a working musician from age 15, performing continuously through his teens and twenties with multiple bands. He recorded two singles that did not chart and held club residencies. However, no material, independently verifiable milestone occurred by age 26. His first album with Elf came in 1972 (age 30), and his fame arrived with Rainbow in 1975 (age 33).

name: Richard Wright
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Pink Floyd in 1965 at age 22 and played on their debut album 'The Piper at the Gates of Dawn' (1967) and two top-20 singles, achieving international recognition as part of one of the most important psychedelic rock bands by age 24.
early_history_summary: Wright grew up in Hatch End, Middlesex, the son of a head biochemist at Unigate Dairies. He was educated at the independent Haberdashers' Aske's School and taught himself guitar, trumpet, trombone, and piano at age 12 while recovering from a broken leg. He took private lessons at the Eric Gilder School of Music, then enrolled at Regent Street Polytechnic in 1962 to study architecture, where he met Roger Waters and Nick Mason. They formed Pink Floyd in 1965 with Syd Barrett.
family_context_summary: Father was head biochemist at Unigate Dairies, providing a middle-class background. Wright attended the independent Haberdashers' Aske's School. His mother encouraged his piano studies after a childhood broken leg.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a biochemist, not in music. No direct family music domain transfer, though mother encouraged piano study.
primary_early_advantage_tags: London 60s music scene, private school education, complementary band members, psychedelic rock wave, self-taught multi-instrumentalist
evidence_summary: Wright benefited from a middle-class upbringing (father was head biochemist at Unigate, independent school education) and grew up in northwest London at the epicenter of the 1960s music revolution. He was self-taught on multiple instruments from age 12 and received private music theory lessons. Meeting Waters and Mason at Regent Street Polytechnic and being joined by Syd Barrett created the complementary team that became Pink Floyd, riding the psychedelic rock wave to international fame by age 24.

name: Gregory Winter

name: Luka Modrić
milestone_by_age_26: Won six domestic trophies with Dinamo Zagreb, was named Player of the Year in the Bosnian league on loan at age 18, and earned a £16.5m transfer to Tottenham Hotspur in 2008 at age 23, becoming a Croatia international since 2006.
early_history_summary: Born in Zadar, Croatia (then Yugoslavia), Modrić grew up in the hamlet of Modrići on the slopes of Velebit mountain. His grandfather was killed by Serbian forces in December 1991, and his family became refugees living in hotels in Zadar during the Croatian War of Independence. He played football on hotel parking lots, joined NK Zadar's academy, and was signed by Dinamo Zagreb at age 16. He was loaned to Zrinjski Mostar in Bosnia at 18, where he won Player of the Year.
family_context_summary: Modrić grew up as a war refugee; his grandfather was killed by Serbian military forces in December 1991. The family lived in dilapidated hotels in Zadar as refugees. His father's occupation is not clearly documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No family football connections found.
primary_early_advantage_tags: war refugee, grandfather killed, football as escape, early academy entry, loan spell in Bosnia, mentor coach
evidence_summary: Modrić's early career was shaped by the Croatian War of Independence, which killed his grandfather and made his family refugees. Football became his escape, playing on hotel parking lots before joining NK Zadar and then Dinamo Zagreb at 16. He was rejected by Hajduk Split for being too small and weak, but persevered through punishing loan spells in Bosnia. Coach Tomislav Basic at NK Zadar was his 'sporting father' who facilitated his move to Dinamo Zagreb. By 23, he had won six domestic trophies and earned a record £16.5m transfer to Tottenham.

name: Fabio Cannavaro
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Serie A debut for Napoli in 1993 at age 19, then won the UEFA Cup and Coppa Italia with Parma by 1999 (age 25-26), and became an Italy international in 1997, all well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Naples to a bank clerk father and a maid mother, Cannavaro grew up in the Rione La Loggetta neighborhood. He was a ball boy at Napoli's Stadio San Paolo at age 13 when the club won its first Serie A title in 1987. He joined Napoli's youth academy, trained alongside Maradona and Ciro Ferrara, and made his first-team debut in 1993 under coach Claudio Ranieri. He moved to Parma in 1995, where he won the UEFA Cup and two Coppa Italia titles.
family_context_summary: Father was a bank clerk who also played football for provincial side Giugliano. Mother worked as a maid. Younger brother Paolo also became a professional footballer. Working-class family in Naples.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father played football at a provincial level and younger brother Paolo became a professional footballer, suggesting a family football culture, though not at elite level.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Napoli youth academy, Maradona era immersion, ball boy to player, father played football, brother professional, working-class Naples, Serie A debut at 19
evidence_summary: Cannavaro's path was defined by immersion in Napoli's youth system during the Maradona era, where he was a ball boy at 13 and trained with the first team alongside Maradona and Ciro Ferrara. His father played football at provincial level and his brother Paolo also became professional, indicating a family football culture. Despite being 5'9" and from a working-class family, he debuted in Serie A at 19 and won the UEFA Cup with Parma by 25. The Napoli youth academy and proximity to elite players like Maradona provided a rare developmental environment.

name: John Bonham
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Led Zeppelin in 1968 at age 20 and played on their debut album released in January 1969, launching one of the most successful rock bands in history well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Redditch, Worcestershire, Bonham began drumming at age 5 using household containers and coffee tins. His mother bought him a snare drum at 10 and his parents bought him a full drum kit at 15. He never took formal lessons. He played in multiple local bands from the early 1960s, including Terry Webb and The Spiders, The Senators, and Way Of Life, building a reputation as one of the best drummers in the Midlands. In 1968, he joined Jimmy Page, Robert Plant, and John Paul Jones to form Led Zeppelin.
family_context_summary: Father Jack was a carpenter who ran the family building business (JH Bonham & Son). Mother Joan ran a local newsagent's shop. The dual family incomes enabled Bonham to attend Wilton House private school. Parents supported his drumming, buying him a snare drum at 10 and a full kit at 15.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family music background documented. Father was a carpenter/builder, mother ran a newsagent's shop.
primary_early_advantage_tags: drumming from age 5, no formal lessons, parents bought drum kit, Midlands music scene, relentless gigging, Led Zeppelin team, hard rock wave
evidence_summary: Bonham was a natural drumming prodigy who started at age 5 without formal lessons and built his skills through relentless gigging in Midlands bands from his mid-teens. His parents, a carpenter father and newsagent mother, supported his passion by buying him drums. By his early twenties, he had a reputation as one of the most powerful drummers in the region. Joining Jimmy Page, Robert Plant, and John Paul Jones in 1968 to form Led Zeppelin created one of rock's greatest complementary teams, riding the hard rock wave to immediate success with their 1969 debut album.

name: John Travolta
milestone_by_age_26: Became a teen idol starring as Vinnie Barbarino in Welcome Back, Kotter (1975) at age 21, then achieved international stardom with Saturday Night Fever (1977) at age 23, earning an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor.
early_history_summary: Born in Englewood, New Jersey, Travolta was the youngest of six children in a family of entertainers. His mother Helen was an actress, singer, and high school drama teacher who inspired all six children to pursue acting. His father Salvatore was a semiprofessional football player turned tire salesman. With his parents' approval, Travolta dropped out of high school at 16 to pursue acting, landing off-Broadway roles (Rain, 1972), Broadway roles (Grease touring company, Over Here! 1974), and his star-making TV role in Welcome Back, Kotter (1975).
family_context_summary: Mother Helen Cecilia (née Burke) was an actress, singer, and high school drama and English teacher who had appeared in radio vocal group The Sunshine Sisters. Father Salvatore was a semiprofessional football player turned tire salesman and partner in Travolta Tire Exchange. All five siblings (Joey, Ellen, Ann, Margaret, Sam) became actors. Irish-Italian American Catholic family.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was an actress and drama teacher who directly trained and inspired all six children to become actors. This is a clear case of family-domain apprenticeship in performing arts.
primary_early_advantage_tags: mother drama teacher, all siblings actors, early NYC theater, dropped out at 16, 70s TV-film boom, disco culture wave
evidence_summary: Travolta's early career was deeply shaped by his family's immersion in performing arts: his mother was an actress and drama teacher who inspired all six children to become actors. He dropped out of high school at 16 with parental support and moved to New York, landing off-Broadway and Broadway roles as a teenager. His proximity to the New York theater scene and then Hollywood, combined with the 1970s TV and film boom, propelled him to teen idol status at 21 and international stardom at 23 with Saturday Night Fever. The family-domain apprenticeship with his mother was the primary early advantage.
